findings.body: When `rfind(' ')` returns `None`, the function returns `head` directly (which is `limit` characters) plus an ellipsis, yielding `limit + 1` characters. The doc comment states the result is "at most `limit` characters". For example, `shorten("abcdef", 5)` (input after trimming) produces `"abcde…"` (6 characters). The test in `a_long_string_stops_on_a_word_boundary` only checks byte length (`out.len() <= 21`) and never triggers the no-space path, so the defect is not caught. The fix should reserve a character for the ellipsis when truncating, e.g., taking `limit.saturating_sub(1)` characters from the text.
findings.title: Ensure shortened string respects the character limit

value.summary: Introduces a `shorten` function that can return a string longer than the requested limit when no space is found, violating its documented contract. This is a concrete bug: `shorten("abcde", 5)` returns `"abcde"` (correct), but `shorten("abcdef", 5)` returns `"abcde…"` (6 characters).
